This page is the plan for WebExtensions in Wren. Phase 1 is written (section 4, "Status of phase 1"). The first target is Bitwarden's browser extension (bitwarden/clients, apps/browser), Manifest V3, Chrome build first, Firefox build second.

Terms used on this page, one per concept:

  • extension: one installed WebExtension package.
  • flavour: chrome or firefox. The flavour decides the URL scheme, the namespaces and the background type.
  • extension origin: the origin of an extension's own documents (chrome-extension://<id> or moz-extension://<uuid>).
  • extension page: a document with the extension origin (popup, options page, offscreen document, a tab).
  • background: the extension's event context. A service worker (Chrome flavour) or an event page (Firefox flavour).
  • world: one JavaScript realm of a document. The main world runs the page's scripts. An isolated world runs the content scripts of one extension.
  • extension context: a realm that has extension APIs: the background, an extension page, an isolated world.
  • router: the object on the loop thread that carries API calls, events, messages and ports between extension contexts.

#1. Scope and non-goals

In scope:

  • Manifest V3 only.
  • Install from an unpacked directory, a .zip file or a .crx file (CRX3). The user chooses the file or the directory.
  • The chrome.* namespace with promises and callbacks. The browser.* namespace with promises for the Firefox flavour.
  • A background service worker (Chrome flavour) and a background event page (Firefox flavour).
  • Content scripts and CSS in isolated worlds. Programmatic injection (scripting).
  • Extension pages: popup, options page, tab, offscreen document.
  • Shell UI: toolbar action button with badge, popup panel, about:extensions, commands, context menus, permission prompts.
  • The API set of section 2. An API outside this set does not exist: chrome.<name> is undefined.

Non-goals of the first phases:

  • No install from the Chrome Web Store or from addons.mozilla.org. No automatic update.
  • No Manifest V2 (browser_action, persistent background pages, blocking webRequest for all requests).
  • No native messaging (runtime.connectNative). Bitwarden uses it only for biometric unlock with the desktop application.
  • No declarativeNetRequest. Wren's content blocker stays the only request filter.
  • No sidePanel (Chrome) and no sidebar_action (Firefox). The manifest keys are parsed and ignored.
  • No privacy API. Bitwarden requests it as an optional permission; the request is refused.
  • No devtools.*, debugger, proxy, downloads, cookies, history, bookmarks, identity, management (except management.getSelf).
  • No messages between two extensions (onMessageExternal, externally_connectable).
  • No extension service worker fetch event for the extension's own pages.
  • No storage.sync to a server. storage.sync is a local area. storage.managed is an empty area.
  • No signature check of a .crx file against a store. The file is treated as an unpacked package from the user.

Bitwarden reads navigator.userAgent to choose its browser type. The Chrome build needs Chrome/ in the user agent and typeof browser === "undefined". The Firefox build needs Firefox/ or typeof browser !== "undefined". Wren's user agent contains Chrome/148.0.0.0 (src/net/settings.odin): the Chrome build detects Chrome, and minimum_chrome_version 134 passes.

#3.2 Registry and profile storage

The registry is one field of page.Pages (Pages.extensions), because every page and worker of the App reads it. The App owns it. It is not a global.

One Extension record holds:

  • id, flavour, version, enabled, the install source (directory, zip, crx) and its path;
  • an image: the parsed manifest, the i18n catalogue, the file index and the compiled match patterns. The image is immutable and reference-counted. Worker threads read it without a lock. A reload makes a new image;
  • the granted permissions and the granted host patterns;
  • the runtime state on the loop thread: the background host, the action state per tab, the context menu items, the alarms, the registered content scripts, the open ports.

Profile files (written through Profile_File, src/browser/profile_writes.odin):

<profile>/extensions.txt                 the list: id, flavour, source, path, enabled, grants, command keys
<profile>/extensions/<id>/package/       the files of a zip or crx install (an unpacked install reads its own directory)
<profile>/extensions/<id>/storage/       local, sync: one store per area (src/idb's file engine: journal, checkpoint)
<profile>/extensions/<id>/state.txt      alarms, context menu items, registered content scripts, the events the background listens to

storage.session is kept in memory by the registry. It is lost when the browser exits or the extension reloads. The web storage of the extension origin (IndexedDB, localStorage, Cache API) goes in the profile's normal stores, keyed by the extension origin. Removing an extension removes its directory and its origin's site data.

Extension id.

  • Chrome flavour with a key in the manifest or a CRX3 public key: the first 16 bytes of the SHA-256 of the DER key, each nibble as a letter a to p.
  • Chrome flavour, unpacked without key: the same encoding of the SHA-256 of the absolute directory path.
  • Firefox flavour: browser_specific_settings.gecko.id identifies the extension. The origin host is a random UUID made at install and kept in extensions.txt.

Flavour. browser_specific_settings.gecko present and no background.service_worker: firefox. Otherwise chrome.

#3.3 Manifest parsing and validation

src/extensions/manifest.odin parses the JSON (comments allowed, as Chrome allows them) into a typed Manifest.

  • An unknown key gives a warning in about:extensions. It is not an error.
  • A wrong type for a known key is an error. The extension does not load.
  • manifest_version other than 3 is an error.
  • A permission that Wren does not implement gives a warning. Its namespace is absent.
  • __MSG_name__ strings are replaced from the catalogue of the UI language, then default_locale.
  • Every file the manifest names must exist in the package and stay inside it.
  • Match patterns (<all_urls>, *://*/*, https://*.example.com/*, file:///*) compile to one matcher (match_pattern.odin). The same matcher serves content_scripts, host_permissions, web_accessible_resources, webRequest filters and tabs.query({url}).
  • Limits, each a preference (extensions.manifest.max_bytes, extensions.package.max_files, extensions.package.max_bytes, extensions.content_scripts.max_entries).

Package readers: a directory is read in place. A .zip is unpacked into package/. A .crx is a CRX3 header followed by a zip; the reader takes the public key from the header and unpacks the zip. An entry with .., an absolute path or a symbolic link is refused.

#3.4 The scheme, its origin, CSP and web-accessible resources

fetch/loader.odin chooses a hop by scheme. Two more schemes go to extension_hop (src/fetch/extension_scheme.odin): chrome-extension and moz-extension. The loader gets the registry through an interface of fetch, as it gets the content blocker (Interceptor): fetch does not import page.

  • Origin. A tuple origin: scheme, host = id or UUID, no port. It is a secure context (url.is_potentially_trustworthy). document.cookie is empty. Storage is keyed by this origin.
  • Lookup. The path is percent-decoded and normalised. A path that leaves the package fails. The file is read on the blocking pool, never on the loop thread. The MIME type comes from the file extension. Responses are not stored in the HTTP cache.

  • Who may load a URL of extension E. One function, extension_may_load(initiator, target):

    1. the initiator has E's origin: yes;
    2. the navigation comes from the address bar, a bookmark or the shell: yes;
    3. the path matches a web_accessible_resources entry and the initiator's URL matches that entry's matches: yes;
    4. otherwise: a network error, the same error as an absent extension. A page cannot tell "refused" from "not installed".
  • use_dynamic_url. Phase 6. The URL host is then a UUID made for the session, not the id.
  • CSP of extension pages. The response carries the manifest's extension_pages policy, or the default script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; object-src 'self'. Wren refuses a manifest policy that allows a remote script source, 'unsafe-eval' or 'unsafe-inline' for scripts. The same policy applies to the background service worker (Sw_Version.csp). src/csp already knows 'wasm-unsafe-eval'.
  • Sandbox pages. A document listed in sandbox.pages gets an opaque origin, the sandbox policy and no extension API.
  • Requests from the extension origin. In fetch's CORS step, a request whose initiator has an extension origin and whose target matches a granted host pattern is same-origin for CORS: no preflight, the response is readable. Cookies follow the normal rules for a cross-site request. A target without a grant gets normal CORS.

#3.5 The background

Chrome flavour: a service worker. page/service_worker.odin keeps registrations, runs each version as a JavaScript worker hosted by a page that shows nothing, starts it for an event and stops it after service_workers.idle_ms. An extension reuses this with four differences, in src/page/ext_background.odin:

  1. The registry creates the registration when the extension is enabled. The scope is the extension origin. No script calls register(). The registration is not written in service_workers.txt: it is derived from extensions.txt.
  2. The script comes from the image (Sw_Version.image). There is no update check and no waiting state. A new version exists only after a reload of the extension.
  3. The loader does not offer requests to it (no fetch event, section 1). install and activate are sent once.
  4. The worker's realm gets the extension APIs (section 3.9). Its API calls are requests to the loop thread, in the form service workers already use (Sw_Reply_Kind.Request answered by Sw_Event_Kind.Answer).

Lifecycle. The router keeps a queue of events per extension. An event for a stopped background starts it. The worker stops after extensions.background.idle_ms (default 30000) with no pending event, no pending API call and no open port. Listeners must be added during the first run of the script. After that run, the router stores the names of the events with a listener (state.txt). A later event with no stored listener does not start the worker. runtime.onInstalled fires after install, update and reload. runtime.onStartup fires at browser start.

Firefox flavour: an event page. A page with the extension origin that shows nothing, with background.scripts loaded in order as classic scripts. It uses the same host as offscreen documents (section 3.8) and the same idle rule. It has a DOM, so the Firefox build needs no offscreen document.

#3.6 Content scripts and isolated worlds

What exists. A Page already holds several Wasm instances that share its DOM (Page.instances). Each call knows its instance (Call.owner). Listeners and timers record their owner instance and are called back in it. A wrapper belongs to one realm and pins its node; a node has one wrapper per realm (docs/frames.md). So an isolated world is one more engine instance on the same Page, with the same handle tag: no call is routed, no value bridge is used.

The new object. Page.worlds: [dynamic]^World (src/page/ext_worlds.odin). A World holds its Js_Realm, its instance index and its extension id. World 0 is the main world (Page.js today). A page has at most one isolated world per extension. All content scripts of that extension in that document share it. A world is created on first need and closes with the page's scope.

What must be split by world. Each item below is keyed by the owner instance today or must become so:

StateRule
Global object, built-ins, prototypesper world (free: another engine instance)
Wrappers and their own propertiesper world (free). A property set by a content script is not visible to the page
Event listeners (addEventListener)per world (Listener.owner). Dispatch order follows registration order across worlds
Event objectsone host event, one wrapper per world (js_events_host.odin already has the case of another realm)
Event handler attributes and on* propertiesthe attribute's handler compiles and runs in the main world only. Each world has its own on* slot
Timers, promises, microtasksper world. The page's microtask checkpoint drains every world's job queue
MutationObserver, IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserverper world: the observer state in Js_Dom_State gets an owner
Custom element registrythe main world only. In an isolated world customElements is null, as in Chrome. Reactions run in the main world
window.postMessage, MessageChannelthe message event goes to the listeners of every world. Each world deserialises its own copy
CustomEvent.detail, event.data of script-made eventscopied by structured clone into the other world; null if it cannot be cloned
Inserted <script> elements, javascript: URLs, document.writerun in the main world, whichever world inserted them
fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket from an isolated worlduse the page's Environment: the page's origin, CORS and cookies. No extension privilege
CSPthe page's CSP does not stop a content script from running or from adding inline styles. Requests it makes follow the page's CSP
window.frames, parent, contentWindowgive the isolated world of the same extension in the other document, or a cross-origin proxy if none exists
Storage (localStorage, indexedDB)the page's origin
Slow-script limit, heap limit, call deadlineper world, the same preferences as a page
Collectiona wrapper of any world pins its node. The grouping of wrappers by tree (js_realm.odin) counts pins of other worlds as outside roots

scripting.executeScript({world: "MAIN"}) runs a file in world 0 with no extension API. It is the only way an extension runs code in the main world, and it needs a host grant for the document.

APIs in an isolated world. runtime (id, getURL, getManifest, sendMessage, connect, onMessage, onConnect, lastError), i18n, storage, dom.openOrClosedShadowRoot, extension.inIncognitoContext. Nothing else.

Injection. src/page/ext_inject.odin, called from the embedder's hooks of the page (realm_started, adopted, parsed, and the load event):

  • For each committed document, the registry gives the matching entries: static content_scripts, scripts registered with scripting.registerContentScripts, and pending executeScript calls. Matching uses the document URL, matches, exclude_matches, include_globs, exclude_globs, all_frames, match_about_blank, match_origin_as_fallback, and the host grants.
  • run_at: document_start: after the document element exists, before any script of the page. document_end: at parsed. document_idle (the default): after document_end, at the load event or 200 ms after parsed, whichever comes first.
  • Script files of one entry run in manifest order, as classic scripts, with the bytecode cache.
  • CSS files are added as author-origin style sheets of the document before the first style pass of document_start. scripting.insertCSS adds one later; removeCSS removes it. The page's scripts do not see these sheets in document.styleSheets.
  • No injection in: extension pages of another extension, about: pages of Wren, view-source:, the documents of Wren's own UI, and hosts in extensions.restricted_hosts.
  • A document whose site has JavaScript switched off still gets content scripts. The switch is about the page's scripts.

#3.7 The router: messages, ports, events, API calls

The router (src/page/ext_router.odin) lives on the loop thread and belongs to the registry. Every extension context registers with it: {extension, kind (background, popup, tab, options, offscreen, content), page, world, tab id, frame id, document id, url, origin}. This record is the MessageSender and the answer of runtime.getContexts. The router fills it; a context cannot forge it.

  • API call. A context sends (method id, call id, JSON arguments). The router checks the context kind and the permission, decodes the arguments, runs the implementation on the loop thread, and answers (call id, result or error). A page realm calls directly. A worker realm sends the call through its worker link.
  • Event. An implementation calls ext_emit(extension, event id, JSON arguments, filter). The router delivers to each context with a listener for that event. A stopped background starts first.
  • runtime.sendMessage. Goes to every extension page and the background of the same extension, not to the sender and not to content scripts. tabs.sendMessage goes to the isolated worlds of that extension in the tab (one frame with frameId, else all frames). The first listener that calls sendResponse, returns true then calls it, or returns a promise, gives the answer. With no receiver, the caller gets the error "Could not establish connection. Receiving end does not exist."
  • Ports. runtime.connect and tabs.connect make a port pair in the router. Each end is an id. postMessage keeps order. disconnect, the close of a page or a world, or the stop of the background fires onDisconnect at the other end. An open port keeps the background alive for extensions.background.port_keepalive_ms after its last message.
  • Payloads. Messages are JSON text, as in Chrome. The Firefox flavour uses structured clone (phase 7).
  • Limits, each a preference: extensions.message.max_bytes (default 64 MiB), extensions.ports.max_per_extension, extensions.events.max_queued, extensions.calls.max_pending. Past a limit, the call fails with an error; nothing is dropped silently.
  • Lifetime. Contexts, ports and pending calls are registered in the scope of their page or worker. scope_close removes them. A late answer for a closed context is dropped (handles, rule 2 of architecture.md).

Tab, window and frame ids: Tab.id and the window's id are already unique in the process. They are mapped to small integers for the API. The top frame is 0. A subframe's id comes from its Navigable id. documentId is a random string per document.

#3.8 Extension pages

An extension page is a normal Page whose URL has the extension origin. Its main world gets the full extension API because its origin equals the extension's. An extension frame inside a web page (Bitwarden's overlay/menu.html) is the same case: the check is the document's origin, not where it is shown.

  • Tab and options page. A normal tab. runtime.openOptionsPage opens options_ui.page or options_page.
  • Popup. A stand-in tab that belongs to no tab strip, as Frame_View is for a frame (frames_shell.odin). It is shown in a toolkit popup panel under the action button. Its size follows the document's content size, between 25 x 25 and 800 x 600 CSS pixels. It closes on a click outside, on Escape, on window.close() and when its tab is no longer the selected tab. Closing it closes its page scope. Context kind: popup.
  • Offscreen document (offscreen.createDocument). A page that shows nothing, hosted like the page that hosts a service worker. One per extension. APIs: runtime only, as in Chrome. It closes with closeDocument, or with the extension. extensions.offscreen.max_lifetime_ms bounds a document whose only reason is CLIPBOARD.
  • Popout window (windows.create({type: "popup"})). A Wren window with one tab and no tab strip, toolbar or address bar. It shows the extension's name and the document title in its title bar.

#3.9 API surface: one description, everything generated

The rule of architecture.md holds: an API starts in api/.

Transport: api/ext.widl, a normal module with generated trampolines and conformance cases:

Ext_info            the context: extension id, flavour, kind, base URL (read once at realm start)
Ext_manifest        the manifest as JSON
Ext_message         i18n: one message by name (the image's catalogue; no loop thread needed)
Ext_call            (method id, JSON) -> Promise<JSON>
Ext_listen          (event id, on/off, filter JSON): tells the router that a listener exists
Ext_eventNext, Ext_eventTake, Ext_eventDone    the next event for this realm, its payload
Ext_respond         the answer to an event that expects one (sendResponse, onAuthRequired)
Ext_portPost, Ext_portClose
Dom_openOrClosedShadowRoot    (the only extension API that takes a node handle)

These imports are linked only into a realm that is an extension context. A page's main world does not have them.

Description: api/ext_<namespace>.widl (ext_runtime.widl, ext_tabs.widl, ext_storage.widl...). The dialect gains three things: [Permission=tabs], [Contexts=(Background, Page, Content)], and event declarations. Structs, enums and optional members describe the JSON shapes. bindgen generates:

  • src/page/ext_api_generated.odin: the method table (id, name, permission, contexts), the JSON decoder of each method's arguments into an Odin struct with type and range checks, the encoder of its result, and the expected prototype of the implementation ext_<namespace>_<method>(c: ^Ext_Call, args: ...) -> (result, Ext_Error). A missing or mistyped implementation does not compile. Implementations are in src/page/ext_api_<namespace>.odin; those that need the shell call through a table of procedures the shell fills (Ext_Embedder, as Sw_Embedder).
  • native/js/odin/ext_gen.odin: the namespace objects built at realm start, the argument normalisation, and the event objects (addListener, removeListener, hasListener).
  • docs/api/ext/: the reference, with the support status of each method.
  • conformance cases: wrong types, missing fields, an absent permission, a wrong context, oversized payloads, for every method.

Calling conventions, written once in native/js/odin/ext_runtime.odin:

  • chrome.*: a method returns a promise. If the last argument is a function, the method calls it with the result and returns undefined. On an error, chrome.runtime.lastError is set during the callback; an unread lastError logs "Unchecked runtime.lastError". Without a callback, the promise rejects with an Error.
  • browser.*: exists only in the Firefox flavour. Promises only. chrome exists there too, with callbacks.
  • A namespace exists only if the image's permissions include it and the context kind allows it. Synchronous members (runtime.id, getURL, getManifest, i18n.getMessage, i18n.getUILanguage) answer from the image without the router.

#3.10 Shell UI

All in src/browser/ext_*.odin, built with the toolkit, driven through the command registry.

  • Action button (ext_toolbar.odin). One button per enabled extension with an action, after the content blocker's icon in address_row. It shows the icon (per tab, action.setIcon with a path or ImageData), a badge (text of at most 4 characters, background colour), and a tooltip (the title). A click opens the popup, or fires action.onClicked when no popup is set. A right click opens a menu: options, manage, remove. More buttons than browser.extensions.toolbar.max_buttons go into an overflow menu.
  • Popup panel (ext_popup.odin): section 3.8.
  • about:extensions (ext_page.odin): the list with name, version, id, flavour, warnings and errors of the manifest; enable, reload, remove; "Load unpacked", "Install from file"; the granted permissions and hosts with a switch per host pattern; the shortcut of each command; the state of the background and a link to its console.
  • Commands (ext_commands.odin). Each manifest command becomes a Command named extension.<id>.<name>, in the category "Extensions", with the suggested key if no command of Wren and no other extension has it. The user changes keys in about:extensions. The command fires commands.onCommand; _execute_action opens the popup. The palette lists them.
  • Context menus (ext_context_menu.odin). The registry keeps a tree of items per extension. context_menu.odin asks it for the items that match the Context_Request (contexts, documentUrlPatterns, targetUrlPatterns). One extension with more than one top-level item gets a submenu with its name and icon. A click fires contextMenus.onClicked with OnClickData and grants activeTab.
  • Prompts (ext_prompts.odin). Install shows the name, the permissions and the host patterns in plain words; the user accepts or cancels. permissions.request shows the added items and needs a recent user action.
  • Notifications: notification_shell.odin already shows system notifications; notifications.create uses it.
  • Developer tools: the background and each extension page are targets of the tools and of wren ctl.

#3.11 Permissions and security model

The extension is a third principal, between the browser and a page. The rules:

  1. An extension is a guest. Every realm of an extension is a Wasm instance with the limits of any guest: the sandbox, the memory cap, the call deadline, the slow-script stop. A trap loses the realm, never the browser.
  2. One gate. Every API call passes ext_call_allowed(context, method) in the router: the extension is enabled, the context kind is allowed, the permission is granted. Every access to a tab or a URL passes ext_host_allowed(extension, url): a granted host pattern, or activeTab for that tab. There is no second path.
  3. The context is known by the host. The router derives extension, kind, tab and frame from the instance that calls. A guest sends no identity.
  4. Host permissions are grants. Install grants the manifest's host_permissions after the prompt. The user can withdraw one pattern in about:extensions. optional_host_permissions need permissions.request. Without a grant for a document: no content script, no executeScript, no tabs.sendMessage target, no url or title in a Tab, no webRequest event, CORS applies.
  5. activeTab. A click on the action button, a command or a context menu item of the extension grants the current document's origin for that tab until it navigates to another origin or closes.
  6. Worlds are isolated. A page script cannot read a content script's variables, wrappers or listeners, and the reverse holds. The two share the DOM tree only. Page scripts can see DOM changes; this is the WebExtensions model.
  7. No extension reaches another. No message, no port, no storage, no file: extension_may_load answers the same error for another extension as for an absent one.
  8. A page reaches an extension only through web_accessible_resources. A page has no chrome.runtime.
  9. Restricted documents. No extension acts on Wren's own pages (about:*), the developer tools, view-source:, another extension's pages, or hosts in extensions.restricted_hosts. tabs data for these tabs has no URL.
  10. Secrets of the browser stay out. No API gives cookies, history, saved form data, the profile path, or the files of the disk. file: documents get content scripts only with the switch "Allow access to file URLs" (off by default).
  11. Requests. webRequest is an observer on fetch.Loader (fetch/observe.odin), filtered by host grants. It cannot block, redirect or change a request. The one exception is onAuthRequired with webRequestAuthProvider: the listener gives credentials for a 401 or 407 challenge, within extensions.webrequest.auth_timeout_ms; then the normal prompt shows.
  12. Private data in logs. The router logs method names, never arguments, messages or storage values.
  13. Bounded resources, each a preference in src/extensions/settings.odin and src/page/ext_settings.odin, registered in src/browser/settings.odin:
PreferenceDefaultReason
extensions.enabledtruethe whole subsystem off: no registry, no hook cost
extensions.max_installed64toolbar and per-document matching cost
extensions.package.max_bytes, max_files512 MiB, 20000a hostile archive
extensions.background.idle_ms30000Chrome's value
extensions.background.max_heap_bytesas javascript.max_heap_bytesBitwarden's SDK and vault live there
extensions.worlds.max_per_document16one engine instance each
extensions.storage.local.max_bytes10 MiB; no limit with unlimitedStorageChrome's value
extensions.storage.session.max_bytes10 MiBChrome's value
extensions.storage.sync.max_bytes, max_item_bytes, max_items102400, 8192, 512Chrome's values
extensions.message.max_bytes64 MiBChrome's value
extensions.alarms.min_period_ms, max_per_extension30000, 500Chrome's values
extensions.context_menus.max_items1000menu build cost
extensions.commands.max_per_extension64palette and shortcut table
extensions.scripting.max_registered1000per-document matching cost

#4. Phases

Every phase ends with something a user can try. Every phase keeps the earlier phases working. Phases 1 to 6 use the Chrome build of Bitwarden. Test fixtures are small extensions in examples/extensions/<name>/; Bitwarden itself is never a test fixture (size, licence, network), it is checked by hand and by the measures of section 5.

#Phase 1: the popup opens and shows the login screen

Scope:

  • src/extensions: manifest.odin, match_pattern.odin, id.odin, package.odin (directory only), i18n.odin, registry.odin, settings.odin.
  • src/fetch/extension_scheme.odin: the hop, extension_may_load rules 1 and 2, the CSP of extension pages, the secure context, the CORS rule for granted hosts.
  • api/ext.widl, the dialect additions in src/tools/bindgen, api/ext_runtime.widl, ext_i18n.widl, ext_storage.widl, ext_tabs.widl (query, get, getCurrent), ext_windows.widl (getCurrent, getAll), ext_action.widl, ext_alarms.widl, ext_permissions.widl (contains), ext_management.widl (getSelf), ext_extension.widl (getViews).
  • src/page: ext_router.odin (calls, events, sendMessage, ports), ext_background.odin (service worker), ext_api_*.odin, ext_storage.odin (local, session, managed; onChanged), ext_settings.odin.
  • native/js/odin: ext_runtime.odin, ext_gen.odin.
  • src/browser: ext_shell.odin (start, stop, the embedder table), ext_toolbar.odin (icon, title, badge), ext_popup.odin, ext_page.odin (about:extensions with "Load unpacked", enable, reload, remove, errors).
  • changelog.d/: one fragment. docs/api/ext/ is generated.

The user can: open about:extensions, load the Bitwarden Chrome build from its directory, see its icon in the toolbar, click it, see the login screen.

Tests:

  • Unit, src/extensions: the manifest (Bitwarden's own manifest.json of both builds as fixtures, each wrong type, each limit), match patterns (the table of Chrome's documentation), the id from a key and from a path, the catalogue (placeholders, fallback to default_locale), path normalisation and traversal.
  • Unit, src/fetch: extension_may_load for each rule; a page gets the same error for an absent and a refused file.
  • Generated conformance cases for ext.widl and every method.
  • Web test web_extensions.odin (no shell): a fixture with a background and a page. Checks: sendMessage with a callback, with a promise, with no receiver (lastError); a port in both directions and its disconnect; storage.local survives a restart of the world; storage.session does not; storage.onChanged; an alarm on the virtual clock; the background stops when idle and starts for a message; a method without its permission is absent.
  • e2e extensions.odin: load the fixture, the button shows, a click opens the popup, the popup's text shows, Escape closes it and frees its page; reload and remove leave nothing allocated.
  • Chrome-world test (chrome_start): the toolbar with 0, 1 and 40 extensions; the badge.
  • The test that breaks this design on day one: the popup calls storage.local.get while the background is stopped and a second popup message is queued. Order and answers must hold with the background starting in between.

#Status of phase 1

Written:

  • src/extensions: settings.odin, manifest.odin, match_pattern.odin, id.odin, package.odin, i18n.odin, storage.odin (the areas), registry.odin (images, the list, grants compiled when they change), json_text.odin.
  • src/fetch/extension_scheme.odin: the hop (files read on the blocking pool), extension_may_load rules 1 to 3, the CSP header of pages and the background, the CORS rule for granted hosts. src/url: the tuple origin and the secure context of chrome-extension: and moz-extension:.
  • api/ext.widl (the transport). src/page: ext_realm.odin (both threads), ext_router.odin, ext_background.odin (a service worker host with Sw_Registration.extension), ext_api.odin (runtime, i18n, storage, tabs, windows, action, alarms, permissions, management, extension). native/js/odin: ext_runtime.odin and ext_api.js.
  • src/browser: ext_shell.odin, ext_toolbar.odin, ext_page.odin (about:extensions with the install prompt).
  • Tests: unit tests of src/extensions and src/fetch/extension_scheme_test.odin; the e2e test src/tools/e2e/extensions.odin with the fixture examples/extensions/hello; Bitwarden's manifests of both builds in examples/extensions/manifests/.

Different from the plan, and why:

  • The API description is one table in src/page/ext_api.odin (methods and events, their permission, their contexts). chrome.* is built from what Ext_info lists for the context, by ext_api.js. The bindgen dialect ([Permission], [Contexts], event) and api/ext_<namespace>.widl are not written: arguments are decoded by each implementation from JSON. This keeps one description; the generated decoders come with the dialect.
  • The popup opens in a tab of its own (ext_open_popup). The panel under the button needs the toolkit to host a page surface in a popup (question 7).
  • extensions.worlds.*, content scripts and web_accessible_resources frames are phase 3 (rule 3 of extension_may_load is written).

Not written yet: the web test web_extensions.odin (the e2e test covers its checks), the chrome-world test of the toolbar, the generated conformance cases per API method, state.txt (the background's listeners are kept in memory only), the overflow menu of the toolbar, icons from ImageData.

#Phase 2: log in and unlock

Scope: what the login and the vault need beyond phase 1. idle (the toolkit's last input time). offscreen (ext_offscreen.odin). tabs.create, update, remove, and the tab events. windows.create (popout), update, remove and the window events. runtime.getContexts, reload, onInstalled, onStartup, openOptionsPage. The clipboard in extension pages with clipboardRead and clipboardWrite and no user action. .zip and .crx install. Fixes for each web platform gap the login shows (expected in crypto.subtle, WebAssembly streaming, IndexedDB, import(), CSS of the Angular popup).

The user can: log in to a Bitwarden account, see the vault, lock, unlock with the master password, copy a password, restart Wren and unlock again, open the popout window.

Tests: web tests for idle on the virtual clock, offscreen (create, one at a time, close, message), tab and window events in order. e2e: the fixture's popup writes the clipboard; a tab opened by tabs.create shows; an install from a zip and from a crx; the session restores the extension. A test server route plays a small login API for a fixture that does fetch, PBKDF2 and AES-GCM in its background, then stores the result.

#Phase 3: autofill

Scope: src/page/ext_worlds.odin and the split of section 3.6 in js_realm.odin, js_events_host.odin, js_observers.odin, js_custom_elements.odin, js_dom_events.odin, timers, message.odin. src/page/ext_inject.odin (static scripts, CSS, run_at, all_frames, globs). api/ext_scripting.widl (executeScript with files and func, both worlds; insertCSS, removeCSS; registerContentScripts, getRegisteredContentScripts, unregisterContentScripts). tabs.sendMessage, tabs.connect. api/ext_webnavigation.widl. ext_dom.widl. web_accessible_resources (rule 3) and sandbox pages. tabs.captureVisibleTab. Host grants in about:extensions.

The user can: open a login page, see Bitwarden's inline menu on the field, choose a login, see the form filled; fill from the popup.

Tests:

  • Web test web_worlds.odin: a variable, a wrapper property and a prototype change of one world are invisible in the other; listeners of both worlds run in order; stopImmediatePropagation crosses worlds; postMessage reaches both; a MutationObserver of each world fires once; an inserted script runs in the main world; customElements is null; a closed shadow root is reachable only through dom.openOrClosedShadowRoot; closing the page with both worlds running leaves nothing allocated; a slow script in an isolated world is stopped and the page lives on.
  • Web test web_content_scripts.odin: run_at order against the page's first script; all_frames; exclude_matches; no injection without a host grant, in about: pages and in another extension's page; CSS applies and is absent from document.styleSheets; executeScript returns the result per frame.
  • e2e: a fixture fills a form of examples/site after a click in its popup; a web-accessible frame shows in the page; a page cannot load a file that is not web-accessible.
  • Measure (-Perf): section 5, the cost of a second world per frame.

#Phase 4: context menus and the save-login bar

Scope: api/ext_contextmenus.widl, ext_context_menu.odin, the hook in context_menu.odin, activeTab. api/ext_webrequest.widl as an observer (onBeforeRequest, onBeforeRedirect, onHeadersReceived, onCompleted, onErrorOccurred, read-only), in src/page/ext_webrequest.odin on fetch.observer_add. api/ext_notifications.widl.

The user can: right-click a field, choose "Bitwarden > Autofill login > (a login)"; copy a password or generate one from the menu; submit a new login and get the bar that saves it.

Tests: chrome-world test of the menu (contexts, patterns, submenu, separators, 1000 items). Web test: onClicked data for a link, an image, a selection, an editable field, a frame; webRequest events in order for a redirect chain, and none for a host without a grant. e2e: the fixture's menu item changes the page.

#Phase 5: keyboard shortcuts

Scope: api/ext_commands.widl, ext_commands.odin, the entries in commands.odin and the palette, the editor of keys in about:extensions, action.openPopup, key conflicts.

The user can: press Ctrl+Shift+L to fill the login, Ctrl+Shift+Y to open the popup, Ctrl+Shift+9 to generate a password; change a key.

Tests: unit tests of key parsing (Ctrl+Shift+Y, MacCtrl, media keys, per-platform keys) and of conflicts. Chrome-world test: the command is in the palette, the key fires it, a key of Wren wins over a suggested key. e2e: the command reaches the background and grants activeTab.

#Phase 6: parity of the Chrome build

Scope: webRequest.onAuthRequired with asyncBlocking. Passkeys through Bitwarden (world: "MAIN" at document_start, the page's navigator.credentials). use_dynamic_url. permissions.request and remove, onAdded, onRemoved. runtime.setUninstallURL, onUpdateAvailable, requestUpdateCheck (answers no_update). storage.sync limits. Incognito answers (false everywhere). Every Bitwarden screen and setting checked by hand with a list kept in docs/extensions-bitwarden.md.

The user can: use every Bitwarden feature except biometric unlock, the side panel and the browser-autofill override.

Tests: web test of the auth provider against the test server's 401 route (credentials given, cancel, timeout then the prompt). e2e of a passkey with the virtual authenticator replaced by a fixture extension.

#Phase 7: the Firefox flavour

Scope: the flavour in the registry, moz-extension://<uuid>/, the browser namespace, the background event page, structured clone for messages, browser.runtime.getBrowserInfo, browser.contentScripts absent in MV3, blocking onAuthRequired with a promise, menus as an alias of contextMenus, Firefox-only manifest keys ignored with a warning. The user agent question of section 6.

The user can: load Bitwarden's Firefox MV3 build and repeat phases 1 to 5 with it.

Tests: the phase 1 to 5 fixtures built once more with browser.* and background.scripts; the same test files run both flavours from one table.

#Later, not planned here

Store install and updates, native messaging, declarativeNetRequest on fetch.Interceptor, sidePanel, cookies, downloads, devtools, Manifest V2.

#5. Risks and how to measure them

RiskWhyMeasureLimit to act on
The Angular popup is slow to openabout 5 MB of script, parsed and run by the interpreter at each open; the popup page is new each timejspage on popup/index.html served from the fixture server: time to first paint, time to the login form; the bytecode cache on and offmore than 1 s to the login form on the reference machine: keep the popup page warm for extensions.popup.keep_warm_ms after close, and check the bytecode cache covers extension files
Unlock is slowPBKDF2 with 600000 rounds or Argon2id in the SDK's WebAssembly, in the backgrounda -Perf web test: crypto.subtle.deriveBits PBKDF2-SHA256 600000 rounds; the SDK's Argon2 in a workermore than 3 s: PBKDF2 must run natively off the loop thread (check bindings_crypto_subtle.odin); Argon2 depends on Wasmtime speed, not on the interpreter
A second realm per frame costs time and memoryBitwarden injects in every frame of every pageper world: start time and committed memory (control_stats), on a page with 0, 1 and 20 frames; the page load benchmark of docs/performance.md with and without Bitwardenmore than 5 % on the load benchmark or more than 8 MiB per world: create the isolated world only when the first script runs, share the pre-initialised image pages copy-on-write, delay all_frames injection for frames out of view
The background restarts too ofteneach start runs 3 MB of scriptcount starts and start time per hour of use, in about:extensionsmore than one start per minute in normal use: raise extensions.background.idle_ms, keep a port open from the popup
Wrapper collection across worlds leaks nodesthe grouping by tree in js_realm.odin was written for one realm per documentthe leak check of every web test of phase 3; e2e memory growth scenario with a content script that adds and removes 10000 nodesany growth after collection fails the test
Web platform gaps in the popup and the content scriptsBitwarden targets Chrome 134run the fixture examples/extensions/probe, which lists every web API of section 2.2 as present or absent; the console of the popupeach absent API is a task before the phase that needs it
API gapsBitwarden calls a method Wren does not have, during startthe router counts calls to unknown methods and logs each name once; about:extensions shows the listthe list must be empty for the flows of the current phase
An extension reads a page it has no grant formany paths: scripts, messages, tab data, requeststhe generated conformance cases; one web test per path of rule 4 in section 3.11, each with a grant withdrawnany pass without a grant is a release blocker
A page detects or attacks an extensionDOM changes are visible; web-accessible frames can be framed and clickedweb tests: a page cannot read the frame, cannot find the id without web_accessible_resources, cannot receive a portas above
A hostile packagezip bombs, path traversal, a huge manifest, 20000 content scriptsunit tests of the package reader and of each limitas above
The dialect change in bindgen growsJSON shapes with unions and optional callbackscount the methods that need hand-written decodingmore than 10 % by hand: extend the dialect, do not add a second generator

#6. Open questions for the user

  1. Which build first. The plan starts with the Chrome MV3 build: its background is a service worker, which Wren has, and Wren's user agent decides what Bitwarden detects. The Firefox build needs an event page and browser.* first. Confirm the order, or reverse phases 1 to 6 and 7.
  2. User agent. Bitwarden's Firefox build looks for Firefox/ in navigator.userAgent in some paths, the Chrome build for Chrome/. Is a per-extension user agent in extension contexts acceptable for the Firefox flavour? The other choice is that Firefox-flavour extensions see Wren's normal user agent and take their Chrome code paths.
  3. Unpacked id. An unpacked Chrome-flavour extension without key gets an id from its path, as in Chrome. Moving the directory changes the id and loses its storage. Accept this, or store a generated key in extensions.txt at first load?
  4. Install prompt. Chrome grants all host_permissions at install. Firefox MV3 treats them as optional and the user grants per site. The plan follows Chrome with a switch per pattern afterwards. Confirm, or choose Firefox's rule for both flavours (Bitwarden then needs a grant per site before autofill works).
  5. Extensions and the content blocker. Do requests made by an extension's pages and background pass through the content blocker? The plan says no for extension contexts and yes for content scripts (they are the page's requests).
  6. Private windows and profiles. Wren has one profile per App. Is "allowed in private windows" needed at all? The plan answers false to every incognito question.
  7. gui_toolkit. The popup needs a toolkit popup panel that hosts a custom-drawn surface and follows its content size. If the toolkit lacks it, it is added there under a new tag, not in Wren. Confirm.
  8. A store later. If store install is wanted after phase 7, the CRX3 signature check and an update service must be planned. This changes nothing before phase 7 but decides whether .crx install keeps the public key now (the plan keeps it).
